descriptionChirho: To seek or search for someone or something, the core Piel meaning of actively looking for a person, object, or abstract goal (Arabic: طَلَبَ/بَحَثَ/فَتَّشَ 'seek/search'; Korean: 찾다/구하다; Swahili: kutafuta; Hindi: ढूँढना/खोजना).

To require, demand, or hold accountable — seeking with authority, implying a claim or exaction rather than mere searching (Arabic: يُطَالِبُ 'to demand'; Swahili: kudai 'to require'; Hindi: माँगना 'to demand'; Korean: 요구하다).

To request, entreat, or plead — seeking favor or petition from a superior, with overtones of supplication (Arabic: الْتَمَسَ/طَلَبَ in petitionary sense; Swahili: kuomba 'to request/pray'; Hindi: प्रार्थना करना/बिनती करना; Korean: 요청하다).
To inquire or ask — seeking information by questioning others (Arabic: سَأَلَ 'to ask'; Swahili: kuuliza 'to inquire'; Hindi: पूछना 'to ask'; Korean: 묻다).

Pual passive: to be sought out, be investigated, or be searched for — the passive counterpart of the Piel active seeking (Arabic: فُتِّشَ/يُطْلَبُ passive forms; Swahili: -tafutwa passive; Korean: 구해지다 passive).
